newsitem.title: SPAIN: Airlines protest at Madrid airport delays.
newsitem.headline: Airlines protest at Madrid airport delays.

text.p: Airlines are demanding that the Spanish authorities act to relieve overcrowding and widespread delays at Madrid's Barajas airport, two groups of independent airlines said in a statement.
"Spanish and foreign airlines request urgent measures to combat the image passengers are forming at the moment of the capital city's airport," they said.
Delays at Barajas have worsened noticeably in the last two months prompting rumours, which Iberia and the airports authority AENA said are unfounded, of a work to rule by handling staff.
An AENA spokesman said only 50 to 55 percent of flights were on time this month on average, compared with an average in 1995 as a whole of 78 percent.

Barajas can handle a maximum of 50 aircraft movements an hour but European air traffic controllers in Brussels are receiving up to 70 requests an hour for clearance from airlines wanting to land or take off in Madrid and inevitably delays occur, AENA said.

AENA says passenger numbers have increased eight percent and aircraft movements 11 percent so far this year compared with last year and is advising airlines not to request more slots at peak hours than those already assigned to them or more than they actually need. Unnecessary requests for slots, airport sources said, is one of the main causes of the delays.
Plans for a third runway, to be ready around the end of the century, are well advanced and the construction contract, worth some 40 billion pesetas ($317 million), should be awarded any day now.

Meanwhile, AENA is considering using other airports in the Madrid area, not currently used by commercial flights, to relieve the overcrowding. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
